glyph_origin: In oracle-bone script, 十 is mostly written as a single vertical stroke; a few examples add a central dot, as in HJ 9204. Later forms added 一, making a cross. One view identifies it as the original graph of 針 (“needle”), later borrowed for 十 (“ten”). See 針. Another view sees it as a knotted-cord or thread-joining form, cf. 什 (三蒼 glosses it as “to gather”), 揖 (the 詩 commentary glosses 揖揖 as “gathered”), 緝 (“to join hemp fibres into thread”), and 輯 (glossed in 說文 as “to collect” and in 爾雅 as “to harmonize”). For the sense of number ten (10), Ideogram (指事) is identified: a vertical stroke, indicating the next digit above one. Unrelated to 支, 卖, 直, 真, 德, 甫, and 七, but related to the original form of 丈.
shuowen: 什 (三蒼 glosses it as “to gather”), 揖 (the 詩 commentary glosses 揖揖 as “gathered”), 緝 (“to join hemp fibres into thread”), and 輯 (glossed in 說文 as “to collect” and in 爾雅 as “to harmonize”).
